requirements.summary: A Core Reader MUST apply every requirement of this document addressed to a reader or verifier, in the order of §10, and MUST refuse a pack that breaks any of them.
Two Core Readers given the same pack, the same trust policy and the same time MUST reach the same verdict, verified or refused.
A Core Reader that does not implement a profile a pack uses (§13) MAY still verify and inspect the pack under this document, and MUST then say which profile it does not implement.
A Core Writer MUST write packs that satisfy every requirement of this document, and MUST NOT write, sign or pass as lint a pack that a reader would refuse by a rule that needs no key (§10).
A Core Writer SHOULD produce the same `META/files.json` and the same archive bytes when it builds the same content twice.
A reader in the **standard** limit class MUST accept every pack within the limits of §18 that satisfies the other requirements, and MUST refuse a pack beyond them.

A reader in the **constrained** limit class (for browsers and small devices) MAY decline a pack beyond limits it states, each no higher than the standard limit; it MUST then report the pack as beyond its limits, not as refused, and MUST NOT verify a pack that a standard reader refuses.
A pack MUST be readable in each of its forms: a folder, an `.ampack` archive (§4) and a member of a pack set (§14.2). A pack's identity is its pack digest, and it MUST be the same in every form.

A reader MUST read a pack in folder form file by file under the same rules as an archive: every file read with a bound, never through a link, never a folder where a file is named, and checked on what was opened rather than only on the path before it was opened.
A reader MUST ignore, at the root of a folder, the version-control files `.git/`, `.gitattributes` and `.gitignore`, and no other file.
When a listed file's hash fails in folder form, a reader SHOULD say when a line-ending conversion to CRLF or a large-file pointer is the likely cause.
A writer that creates a pack folder SHOULD write a `.gitattributes` of `* -text -filter -diff`.

The entries of an archive MUST be contiguous from offset 0, with no prefix, suffix, gap or overlap; the archive MUST end with the end-of-central-directory record, with no comment and no trailing bytes.
Each local header MUST equal its central-directory entry (name, method, sizes, CRC, flags).
An entry MUST use method 0 (stored) or 8 (deflate). An entry MUST NOT use data descriptors, encryption, extra fields or a comment; the archive MUST NOT hold directory entries, and MUST NOT use ZIP64.
Entries MUST be sorted by name, each name at most once; every entry MUST carry the fixed time 1980-01-01 00:00 and external attributes 0.
Every entry name MUST be a path in the grammar of §5.
A deflate stream MUST be valid, MUST end with its final block, and MUST end exactly where its entry's bytes end.

A reader MUST count inflation against the entry's declared size and refuse an entry that inflates beyond it, MUST refuse an entry whose declared compression ratio exceeds 250:1 before inflating it (a deflated entry of 0 bytes that declares content included), and MUST check every entry's CRC.
An archive MUST hold at most 4,096 files, each at most 64 MiB, at most 256 MiB in total, and MUST be at most 512 MiB.
A reader MUST verify and import from the same bytes it read, and MUST NOT extract an archive before it is verified.
A path MUST be 1 to 255 characters of at most 8 segments separated by `/`; each segment MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}` (so at most 100 characters) and MUST NOT end with a dot.
A segment whose part before its first dot is, in upper case, one of the device names below MUST be refused.
Two files, two folders, or a file and a folder whose paths differ only by case MUST be refused, and so MUST a file named like a folder.
A JSON text MUST be UTF-8 without a byte order mark and MUST NOT contain a carriage return.
An object MUST NOT repeat a key, at any depth.

Every string and every object key MUST be in Unicode Normalization Form C, decided by the Unicode 15.0 tables whatever the platform's own normalizer or globalization mode, and MUST NOT hold a lone surrogate.
A string or object key MUST NOT hold more than 30 combining marks in a row, counted as UAX #15 (Stream-Safe Text Format) counts them, on each character's NFKD decomposition.
Every number MUST be finite and representable as an IEEE 754 double, and every integer MUST be within ±(2^53 − 1).
Arrays and objects MUST NOT nest deeper than 64.
A listed JSON file and a JSONL line MUST each be at most 1 MiB.
`META/files.json` and `META/lock.json` MUST be in RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form and hold integers only; a reader MUST refuse unless the bytes equal the canonical form of their parse.
A listed `.json` or `.jsonl` file under `assets/` MUST still be checked in the JSON profile, as every listed JSON file is.

A date and time MUST be RFC 3339 written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, with an optional fraction of 1 to 7 digits, then `Z` or an offset `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` whose minutes are below 60 and whose size is at most 14 hours, in ASCII digits; two times MUST be compared to 100 ns.
Base64 MUST be strict: the standard alphabet and padding only, no white space.
A version MUST be a SemVer 2.0 version in ASCII digits, at most 256 characters, each numeric part fitting 64 bits, with no leading zero in a numeric prerelease identifier.
A pack MUST hold `META/files.json`, at most 2 MiB.
`META/files.json` MUST be an object holding exactly the fields below, with `format` `agentmemory.pack.files/1.1`, an `id` in the grammar of §11.3, a `version` (§6), and `files`, an array of entries.
Each entry of `files` MUST hold exactly `path` (a path, §5), `length` (a non-negative integer) and `sha256` (64 lowercase hexadecimal digits); entries MUST be sorted by path, each path at most once.

A pack MUST hold exactly the listed files, apart from `META/files.json` itself and the files under `META/signatures/` and `META/attestations/`; a listed file missing, or an unlisted file present, MUST refuse the pack.
Every listed file MUST have exactly its listed length and SHA-256.
The pack digest MUST be computed over the exact bytes of `META/files.json`, never over a re-serialization; signatures cover those exact bytes, and verifying MUST NOT re-canonicalize them.
The `id` and `version` of `META/files.json` MUST equal those of `pack.json`.
Every file under `META/signatures/` that is not a timestamp token (§8.4) MUST be an envelope; any other file there MUST refuse the pack.

An envelope MUST be a DSSE envelope holding exactly `payloadType`, `payload` and `signatures`; `payloadType` MUST be `application/vnd.in-toto+json`, `payload` strict base64, and `signatures` a non-empty array whose entries each hold exactly `keyid` (64 lowercase hexadecimal digits) and `sig` (strict base64 decoding to 1 to 72 bytes). This one closed shape holds for every envelope the format defines.

The payload MUST be an in-toto Statement v1 holding exactly `_type`, `subject`, `predicateType` and `predicate`; `subject` MUST name exactly one subject, `META/files.json`, holding exactly `name` and `digest` with exactly `sha256`, the SHA-256 of this pack's `META/files.json`.

A pack role's predicate MUST hold exactly `role`, `id`, `version` and `signedAt`; its `predicateType` MUST be `urn:agentmemory:pack:<role>:v1` for a signing role of §8.2, `id` and `version` MUST be this pack's, and `signedAt` MUST be a UTC time written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
An envelope that does not sign this pack's list in a known role MUST refuse the pack.
A signature MUST be ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the DSSE pre-authentication encoding of the payload, encoded as strict DER; a signature that is not strict DER MUST NOT count.
A signature entry by a key the trust policy does not hold MUST be ignored; an entry by a trusted key that does not verify, or does not count by §9.2, MUST be reported and MUST NOT count.
A pack MUST carry, for every role the trust policy requires (the publisher, unless the policy names others), at least one signature that counts; otherwise the pack MUST be refused.
Curator and assurer envelopes MAY be carried; a reader MUST report them and they gate nothing unless the trust policy requires their role.
An envelope MUST be at most 64 KiB and hold at most 16 signature entries; a pack MUST carry at most 16 envelopes; a reader MUST hash each envelope's pre-authentication encoding once.

Beside an envelope `<envelope>`, a pack MAY carry at most one timestamp token `<envelope>.tsr`, at most 64 KiB. A reader of this version MUST keep it and MUST NOT judge its content: it checks the token's name, place and size only, and nothing in it is trusted or shown.
A token beside no envelope, or larger than 64 KiB, MUST refuse the pack.
A writer that writes a new envelope by the same key MUST drop the old token beside it.
A key's id MUST be the SHA-256 of its DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

A trusted key MUST be scoped by id prefixes and by roles: it MAY sign only for pack ids its prefixes cover, by whole segments (a prefix covers the id equal to it and the ids below it at a `.`, never a lookalike), and only in its roles.
A trusted key MAY carry a validity window (`notBefore`, `notAfter`).
A key in the revoker or evaluator role MUST hold that role alone.

A verified signature MUST count only when all of these hold: its key is in the role the statement names; its prefixes cover the pack id; the signing time is not before `notBefore` and the time now is not before `notBefore`; the signing time is not after `notAfter`; the time now is not after `notAfter`; the signing time is not more than 5 minutes after now; and the key is not revoked.
The rule of R-CORE-061 MUST be the one rule for every signature the format defines: pack envelopes, publication receipts and certificates alike (each with its own role).
A host MUST be able to revoke pack digests and keys; a revoked digest MUST refuse the pack, and a signature by a revoked key MUST NOT count.
Revocations distributed to hosts MUST be signed documents by a key in the revoker role, with an issue time and an expiry; revocations MUST be added, never removed.
When the host's revocations have expired, a reader MUST refuse every pack until they are refreshed.
A revoker's prefixes MUST NOT scope what it revokes: revokers are global.

A loaded pack MUST be valid until the first of: its own `validUntil`, its composite's and set's, the revocation list's expiry and its signing keys' expiry. It MUST be valid through that instant, and off after it.
A reader MUST refuse a pack whose `validUntil` has passed.

A host MUST keep a ledger that survives uninstall, recording for each id the highest version ever installed and for each (id, version) its digest, and MUST refuse a downgrade, or a known version with another digest, unless the operator says so. Its document is `host/ledger.md`.

A reader MUST verify in this order, refusing at the first rule broken: (1) the archive profile and the paths; (2) `META/files.json`, the listed files and their hashes, the signature folder and the envelopes; (3) the signatures and trust; then (4) the JSON profile of every listed file, `pack.json` and its kind, the card, the records, revocation and lifetime, and each implemented profile's rules (federation among them); and last (5) the ledger. Only then MAY one record reach a store.

Before the signatures hold, a reader MUST NOT parse anything but `META/files.json` and the envelopes. This holds for every reader and every load path, not only for a verifier: a host that must know a pack's kind to choose how to load it MUST read the kind only once the signatures hold.
Every parser MUST refuse more than its bound, whoever calls it: the files list 2 MiB, an envelope 64 KiB, `pack.json`, a card and a lock 1 MiB.

Every rule a reader applies before any trust MUST be applied as one check by every door that reads a pack before it is trusted (lint, every writer's read-back, every command): the paths, the files list and the content it lists, the signature folder, each envelope a DSSE envelope of a pack role's statement signing this list for this pack (whether its keys count is judged once trust is applied), the JSON profile, `pack.json` and the kind; for a set, the member rules of §14.2.

A door that acts on a pack under a host's policy (countersigning, locking, building a set, and diffing or scanning given a policy) MUST verify the pack whole: a set with every member it carries, never on its outer signature alone.
`pack.json` MUST be an object whose fields are among those below (at the reader's own minor; for a later minor, see §12).
At the reader's own minor or an earlier one, a field of `pack.json` this document does not define MUST refuse the pack, naming the field.
A value of `kind`, `tier`, `protection` or `code` outside the closed values above MUST refuse the pack, at every minor.

A field of `pack.json` of the wrong type MUST be refused, never read as absent. The fields below MUST be strings; `requires` and `display` MUST be objects; `display.icon`, when present, MUST be a string; `contains` and `containableBy` MUST be arrays of ids.

An id (of a pack, set or composite, and every entry of `containableBy`) MUST have at least three lowercase segments separated by `.`, each starting with a letter and holding letters, digits and inner hyphens, and MUST be at most 64 characters. Patterns that match it MUST anchor at the very end of the text, never before a final line break.
A pack's id MUST be in its publisher's namespace, as the trust policy scopes the publisher's key (R-CORE-058).

`display.title` MUST be at most 60 characters and `display.description` at most 300; `display.color` MUST be `#RRGGBB`; an icon MUST be a PNG under `assets/`, 16 to 512 pixels a side and at most 64 KiB, and MAY appear only on a knowledge pack.

`source` MUST be an object whose members are among `repository`, `commit` and `builtAt` (each optional), each a string of 1 to 200 characters; `builtAt` MUST be a time (§6) and `commit` 7 to 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
`validUntil` MUST be a time (§6).
A member of `extensions` MUST be ignored, unless `extensions.critical` names it.
`extensions.critical` MUST be a list of distinct names of members `extensions` holds (never `critical` itself); a name the reader does not understand MUST refuse the pack.

`format` MUST be `agentmemory.pack/1.` followed by a minor from 2 to 999 written without leading zeros. A reader MUST state the minor it implements (this document: 2). Minors 0 and 1, another major, and any other spelling (such as `1.02`, `1.2.0`, a trailing line break, or digits of another script) MUST NOT be read.
A pack of the reader's own minor or an earlier one MUST be read strictly: every field of `pack.json` is one this minor defines, or the pack is refused, naming the field.

In a pack of a later minor, a top-level field of `pack.json` the reader does not know MUST be ignored and the reader MUST say so, unless the pack lists it in `critical`, which MUST refuse the pack as needing a newer reader.

`critical` MUST hold 1 to 64 distinct names of fields this `pack.json` holds; naming a field it does not hold, or `critical` itself, MUST refuse the pack. A name the reader does not understand MUST refuse at any minor; naming a field the reader knows is allowed and changes nothing.

The values of a known field MUST stay closed at every minor, and every document a reader defines MUST keep its exact shape for all of 1.x. New meaning MUST come as a new `pack.json` field or a new file, never as a new value or a new member of a known document; a changed document is a new file or a new major.

A listed file the reader does not define MUST be inert at every minor: no reader reads it as a declaration. A later minor that gives a file meaning MUST declare it with a `pack.json` field, critical where an older reader must not skip it.
The identity and trust layer MUST stay fixed for the whole major: the archive profile, `META/files.json`, the envelopes and their statements, the signing roles and the attestation slot.

A field introduced by a later minor that bears on whether or how a pack is trusted, protected, runs code, is federated, nests, expires, or is switched on by a trial MUST be listed in `critical` by its writer; a reader of that minor MUST refuse a pack that uses such a field without listing it.
A writer MUST refuse to sign a `pack.json` of a later minor than it writes.
A reader MUST derive a pack's profiles from what it holds by the registry's profile map, in the registry's order, and two readers MUST derive the same profiles for the same pack.

A host MUST refuse to load a pack that uses a profile the host does not implement, and a profile the registry marks not implemented MUST be refused with the refusal words the registry gives it. A declared restriction never loads as if it were absent.
A verifier SHOULD report the profiles it derived for a verified pack.
A profile introduced by a later minor MUST arrive as a critical `pack.json` field or a file a `pack.json` field declares (§12).
`pack.json` MUST name a kind.
A `knowledge` or `snapshot` pack MUST hold records under `records/` (files `records/*.jsonl`); a `definition` pack MUST hold none.
A `composite` or `set` pack MUST NOT declare `sdk`, `requires` or `containableBy`: its members carry their own.

A host MUST import a knowledge pack's records only through its pack import, which holds at most 5,000 records in at most 16 files, a line at most 64 KiB and nesting at most 8, shared types only, relations only between two types of the same pack, and no `requires.modules`.
A set MUST carry its members under `packs/`, every file under `packs/` MUST be inside a member folder `packs/<id>/`, and the members MUST be exactly those the set's `contains` names.
Each member MUST verify on its own, by every requirement of this document; a member that does not MUST refuse the set. The set's own signature binds the members together.
The pack in `packs/<id>/` MUST have the id `<id>`; a member MUST NOT have the set's own id; and a member MUST NOT be a set.
A set MUST NOT hold an archive inside an archive.
A record file MUST be JSONL: one JSON object per line, each line ending with a line feed (including the last), no empty line, each line in the JSON profile.
A record MUST be an object of `type`, `key`, `properties` and `links`, as the record's module declares them.
The member `labels` is reserved: a record that carries it MUST be refused until a profile defines how a host enforces labels.
A host that writes records it read from elsewhere MUST put their text in NFC as it writes, and MUST refuse text that still is not in NFC.

When present, `card.json` MUST be read strictly: `format` `agentmemory.pack.card/1`, the fields above only (an unknown field MUST refuse the pack), `owner.name`, `intendedUse` and `limitations` required, each of its type and within its length.
Card lengths MUST be counted in characters, and card text MUST be display-safe (R-CORE-126).
A writer SHOULD write a template card when it creates a pack, and SHOULD advise while a card is still the template or when a knowledge or definition pack carries no card.

`META/attestations/` MUST hold only `<stem>.certificate.dsse.json` and `<stem>.erasure.dsse.json` files and `<stem>.aef/…` runs, where a stem matches `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`; any other file there MUST refuse the pack.
The slot MUST hold at most 8 certificates, each at most 64 KiB; a run MUST travel beside its certificate's stem, with at most 256 files and 8 MiB.
A Core Reader MUST check the slot's shape and bounds only, and MUST NOT trust anything in it: an untrusted or malformed certificate MUST NOT refuse the pack.
A writer that rebuilds a pack with changed content MUST drop its attestations.

Every file a reader or a host reads (an archive, a revocation list, a trust policy, a key, a receipt, a certificate, an evidence file, the ledger, an activation record) MUST be read with its bound, never through a link and never a folder where a file is named, checked on what was opened; a pipe or a device MUST be read with the same bound, the limit checked before each block is kept; a file that cannot be read MUST be refused.

A unit-bearing field of a format document (the registry's `units.fields`) MUST be an integer written as one (digits only: no fraction and no exponent, so `800000.0` and `8e5` are not), within ±(2^53 − 1). Its name ends in its unit: `Micro`, millionths of one; `Permille`, thousandths from a closed set; `Ms`, whole milliseconds. It MUST be within the range, or among the values, the registry gives it.

Wherever this specification bounds text, the length MUST be counted in characters (code points); wherever it orders text, the order MUST be by code point, except JCS's order of object keys (R-CORE-032).

A record's `type` MUST be a type the pack's `ontology.json` declares, or a built-in type; a link's `relation` MUST be a relation declared from the record's type, or a built-in relation from a built-in type.
A property MUST be of one of these types:
A pack MAY use these types and relations without declaring them; a record of a built-in type MUST hold only its properties, each required one present:

A type MAY name one of its string properties as its `text`, the record's main text (a built-in type names its own, above); it MUST be in NFC (R-CORE-027), and its length is bounded, in characters, by the property's `maxLength`.
A type MAY declare a `memoryKind`, one of these, for mapping and display only: no rule of this specification depends on it.

A record MAY carry `validFrom` and `validTo` (when it is true in the world, `validTo` exclusive and after `validFrom`), `expiresAt` (when a host stops using it, true or not) and `reviewBy` (when a person should check it), each an instant in UTC to the second (`yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`), and `supersedes`, 1 to 8 distinct keys of other records of its type in the same pack. A record is **live at T** when its carrier is live (R-CORE-067) and `validFrom <= T < validTo` and `T < expiresAt`, each bound absent meaning none.

A type MAY declare a `lifecycle`: `pinned`, whose records carry no `expiresAt`, or `refreshes`, with `ttlDays` (1 to 36,500), whose records state `validFrom` and, without a `validTo`, end `ttlDays` after it.

A record superseded by another ends where the other begins: its `validTo` is the earlier of its own and the other's `validFrom`, and when the other states none, it is never live. A record MUST be superseded at most once, the keys MUST name records the pack holds, and supersession MUST NOT form a cycle. A reader resolves each record's effective life this way before it stores the record, so a store keeps instants and no rule.

An erasure MUST be a DSSE envelope of an in-toto statement of predicate type `urn:agentmemory:pack:erasure:v1` whose predicate holds exactly `id` (the pack id, all its versions), `issuedAt` (an instant in UTC to the second, in ASCII digits), `reason` (`withdrawn`, `incorrect`, `harmful` or `legal`), `salt` (32 lowercase hexadecimal characters) and `records`, 1 to 256 distinct objects of `type` and exactly one of `key` (a string of 1 to 1,024 characters) or `keyHash` (64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, the SHA-256 of the salt, a colon and the key in UTF-8), so a notice need not reveal what it erases. It travels in a pack's attestations as `<stem>.erasure.dsse.json`, the stem its signer's key and issue time, or on its own.

A verifier MUST hold an erasure only when a signature verifies by a key the trust policy names as `publisher` or `revoker` for the pack's id, valid at `issuedAt` and now, and the erasure names that pack. For a federated pack (§14) the key MUST also be bound to the pack's publisher WebID, as its publisher signature is.

A host MUST apply every erasure it holds for a pack before it writes any of that pack's records, from any version: each erased record's every version, and its content, MUST leave the store, and the host MUST keep a tombstone of the pack, the type, the salt and the key's hash, never the key.

A host MUST NOT write, hold or offer a record a tombstone or an erasure it holds names, whichever version or copy brings it; a link into an erased record goes with it, and the record that held it is still written. A host that holds an erasure it has not yet applied to its store MUST still leave the records it names out of every read. An erasure for a pack names only the records that pack carried (its own, or a snapshot's it carried), never another's of the same module, type and key.

On request, a host MAY sign a receipt that it applied an erasure it verifies: a DSSE envelope of an in-toto statement of predicate type `urn:agentmemory:pack:erasure-receipt:v1` naming only the erasure statement's identity and when it was applied.

Text a pack shows to a person (its card, `display.title`, which is one line, `display.description`, the federation `purpose`, and every text a verifier checks as one) MUST be display text: display-safe, holding no code point in these ranges, fixed at Unicode 15.0 whatever the platform's own tables; not blank (some character outside Unicode's White_Space); and, when it is one line, holding no line feed, tab, line separator (U+2028) or paragraph separator (U+2029). The ranges are the C0 and C1 controls but line feed and tab, every format character but ZWNJ and ZWJ (so every bidi control and the zero-width space), private use and surrogates.

A card MAY hold `whenToUse`, written for the model: what the pack knows and when to ask it, display text of at most 400 characters. Only a knowledge or definition pack's travels into the module the host composes, in its declarations: a snapshot runs its definition's, and a composite or set composes its members'. A host MAY show it on every turn; one that does MUST pass it through its admission of untrusted content first (R-HOST-056) and put it in a frame naming the module, its version and the type `whenToUse` (R-HOST-053): it is the pack's own words, data, never an instruction. A trial MUST count those framed bytes as the pack's fixed cost per turn (R-TRIAL-056), whether or not the host shows or admits it. A listing that returns it as data (`pack_list`) MUST return the composed module's.
A Walk Host MUST implement Ampack Core as a Core Reader, and every requirement of this document.
Two Walk Hosts that follow §5 MUST offer the same records in the same order for the same anchors, question and records (budgets aside), whatever store holds the records.

`ontology.json`, `views.json`, `traversal.json` and `evals/trial.json` MUST be the matching members of the module manifest, whose JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) is `agentmemory.module.v1alpha1.schema.json`; the schema is normative for shape, names and ranges.
An integral number MUST be read as an integer whether written `2` or `2.0`, the numeric `min` and `max` of an `int` property included.
The module files MUST be read strictly: a member the schema does not define MUST refuse the pack.

A host MUST also apply the rules the schema cannot state: an anchor names an owned string property; anchors are unique by (type, property) and relations by (name, direction); a traversal relation is an owned relation and never into `core:` entities; a hub names an owned type; `containableBy` names module ids or namespaces in the id grammar; a view reads only declared types; the label and relation prefixes hold; reserved names are not used; display texts hold no control characters.

The schema and the host's validator MUST reach the same verdicts on the edges: 16 and 17 traversal relations, 16 and 17 anchors, a traversal with neither, trial tasks 9, 10, 200 and 201, an upgrade tolerance of -0.01, 0, 0.05, 0.5 and 0.6, `hops` written 2.0, an `int` bound written 2.0, and a `containableBy` entry that is not an id.

Where a field is absent, a host MUST use these defaults: traversal `maxItems` 4 and `hops` 2; anchor `match` `exact` and `kind` `path`; relation `direction` `out`, `weightMicro` 800,000 and `fanOut` 8.
A traversal MUST declare at most 16 relations and at most 16 anchors; `maxItems` MUST be 1 to 16, `hops` 1 to 3, `fanOut` 1 to 32, and `weightMicro` 1 to 1,000,000 (R-CORE-119).
An anchor declaration's `kind` MUST be `path` or `symbol`; `key`, `entity` and `text` are reserved and MUST be refused.

A host MUST assemble its module manifest from a pack by a pure mapping: `pack.json` (`id`, `version`, `sdk`, `requires`, `display`, `containableBy`), `ontology.json`, `views.json`, `traversal.json`, `evals/trial.json`, and the record files as seed; then validate the manifest as it validates any manifest.
An assembled module manifest MUST be at most 128 KiB and nest at most 32 deep.

A host MUST refuse a record its module's ontology does not admit, naming the file and line, before any record is imported; a link through a relation the ontology does not declare MUST be such a problem, never a failure of the host.
A `definition` pack MUST hold declarations only (ontology, traversal, views, trial); its records MUST come from the host's importer for that kind, never from `records/`.

A `snapshot` pack MUST hold a definition's records for one source at one commit, at most 250,000 records, of shared types only, and MUST require exactly its definition; a host MUST refuse a snapshot for another definition or a version outside the definition's range.
A host MUST import a snapshot's records through its snapshot import path, which writes only what changed, and MUST NOT compose a snapshot as a module.
A snapshot pack without a source commit MUST take its version as its source.
A host SHOULD report a snapshot pack against its own commit as fresh, stale (with how many commits behind) or unknown; only a snapshot that names a commit can be judged.
Records imported from a snapshot MUST keep the pack that carried them, with its signer.
A module whose `validUntil` passes while it is loaded MUST contribute nothing from then on, and SHOULD report an omission naming the date.
Every number in the walk MUST be an IEEE 754 double.
Case folding MUST be ASCII only: `A`–`Z` fold to `a`–`z` and nothing else folds (so `Ä` and `ä`, `µ` and `μ`, `İ` and `i` stay apart). Every implementation MUST fold this way, store filters included.
White space MUST be space, tab, CR, LF, form feed and vertical tab only (a non-breaking space is a character like any other); a digit MUST be `0`–`9`; anything else compares as it is.
The walk MUST run for live requests only, never for a request with an as-of time.
Wherever records tie, they MUST be ordered by module id, then type, then key, each compared by code point, then by version id. Every tie in §5 MUST be broken by this order.

Anchors MUST be taken by one intake at every entry point (a host, a server mounting packs, its remote operations, pack tests), in request order; an entry point MUST pass anchors as given and leave every step to the intake, and what it echoes, or asks a question about, MUST be the list the intake took.

The intake MUST take each value in turn: (1) a value longer than 2,048 characters is dropped before any work; (2) the value is normalized by its kind, a path as in R-WALK-037 and a symbol trimmed of ASCII white space; (3) it is put in NFC by the format's own Unicode 15.0 tables, the same ones the JSON profile checks with, whatever the host's globalization mode; (4) a value that is then empty, longer than 512 characters, or holds a lone surrogate is dropped; (5) the values are made distinct by (kind, value); (6) the first 32 are kept.
The intake MUST be idempotent: what it takes, taken again, is the same list.
An entry point MAY refuse a request of more than 256 anchors.
Stored text MUST be in NFC: a record's key, its string properties, its link targets and the keys it replaces, so that an anchor in any normal form reaches the record it names.

Only modules that declare `traversal` and an ontology, and are live (not past `validUntil`: valid through that instant, off after it), MUST take part; a module that is not live MUST neither seed, steer nor offer.

The question's words MUST be found thus: put the question in NFC by the format's tables (as given when it holds a lone surrogate); split identifiers where a lower-case letter or digit meets an upper-case letter; lower-case; take the runs of `[a-z0-9]` (after ASCII folding); keep those of 3 to 40 characters that are not in the common list below; distinct, in order, at most 16.

A record's *matches* MUST be how many of the words occur (ordinal substring) in the ASCII-folded join, by single spaces, of its type's text properties: the string properties its `render` template names, in template order, distinct; without a template, every string property in ordinal name order.

Seeds MUST be found for each module in dependency order (levels of the dependency graph, ordinal by id within a level) and, within it, for each declared anchor `{type, property, match, kind}` in declaration order: the anchors of that kind are matched against the property's value of every live record of the type in the request's scope.
A store MUST scan every candidate, none left out before matching (it MAY scan a superset); only the time budget MUST stop the scan, in every store alike.
A store MUST return the matches only, best first (the match quality below, then key and id, ordinal), at most 257: the 256 a walk keeps and one to say there are more.

A path MUST be normalized before it is compared, in one pass: each `\` read as `/`, trailing ASCII white space dropped, then the leading run of ASCII white space, `/` and `./` dropped (so `./ a` is `a`). A normalized path MUST normalize to itself.
Two paths MUST be equal when they are equal after ASCII folding. A value, or a piece of one, that normalizes to nothing MUST match nothing.

Qualities and scores are integers in millionths. `exact` MUST give 1,000,000 when the normalized value is not empty and equal to the normalized anchor, else 0. Every `exact` declaration MUST normalize as a path and compare ASCII-folded, a symbol's included (so `removepackasync` seeds `RemovePackAsync`).

`prefix` MUST split the value on space, tab, CR, LF, `,` and `;`, take each pattern without its trailing slashes, and give 1,000,000 when equal; when the anchor starts with `pattern/`, 500,000 + ⌊300,000 × min(depth, total) / total⌋, where depth = slashes in the pattern + 1 and total = slashes in the anchor + 1; else 0.

`glob` MUST split as `prefix` does. Without `*` or `?`, a pattern MUST be a prefix match (a pattern ending `/`) or an exact match. With them, `*` MUST match within a segment, `?` one character in a segment, `**/` zero or more folders and a bare `**` anything, matched over the ASCII-folded pattern and anchor, the whole anchor from its first character to its last; a match MUST give 700,000.

`name` MUST split on CR, LF, `,` and `;` only, trim each piece of ASCII white space, and compare ordinally and case-sensitively: 1,000,000 when equal; 900,000 when the simple names are equal and not empty.

A simple name MUST be found thus: the text after the last space; without trailing `#`, `.`, `/`, `:` and `!`; cut at the last `(` when it ends with `)`; then what follows the last `/`, `#`, `.` or `:` (so `…/Neo4jModuleStore#` gives `Neo4jModuleStore`, and `…#RemovePackAsync().` gives `RemovePackAsync`).
A record's seed score MUST be its best quality over every pattern and anchor; 0 is no seed.

Anchors MUST be normalized once; a value's pieces MUST be read and prepared as the first anchor reaches them and kept for the others; a glob MUST be matched by stepping positions through the anchor, with no regular-expression engine.
A blank value (empty or ASCII white space only) MUST cost nothing and match nothing. Any other value MUST be read piece by piece from its start, as below.

*Reading.* A piece MUST run from where reading stopped to the next separator of its match (`glob`, `prefix`: space, tab, CR, LF, `,` and `;`; `name`: CR, LF, `,` and `;`; `exact`: none, so the whole value is one piece); form feed and vertical tab MUST NOT separate. Reading a piece MUST cost its characters, separator excluded, plus 1. A piece MUST then be trimmed of the six ASCII white-space characters; one empty after trimming is read and charged, never prepared or compared. Reading MUST stop at the value's end: a separator at the very end opens no piece.
*Preparing.* Preparing a non-empty piece MUST cost 32 plus 4 for each character of the trimmed piece, or plus 6 for each when the match is `glob`, whether or not that piece holds a wildcard.
*An equality.* An equality of two strings MUST cost 1, plus their length when their lengths are equal.

*Comparing.* Comparing a prepared piece with an anchor MUST cost: for `exact`, an equality of the folded paths when the piece's path is not empty, nothing otherwise; for `prefix`, 1, then nothing more when the piece's folder (folded path, trailing `/` removed) or the anchor's path is empty, else an equality, then twice the folder's length when the anchor's folded path is longer and has `/` just past it; for `glob`, 1, then, for a piece with `*` or `?`, the glob steps below when the anchor's path is not empty, and for a piece without, nothing more when the piece's folded path or the anchor's path is empty, else a `prefix` comparison when the piece ends with `/`, else an equality; for `name`, an equality of the piece and the trimmed anchor, and when that fails and the piece's simple name is not empty, an equality of the simple names.

*Glob steps.* A pattern's tokens MUST be what it compiles to: each literal character and each `?` is one token; `**/` is one token, `**` not before `/` one, `*` one. Of two wildcard tokens side by side, a `**` not before `/` absorbs the other, and two of one kind are one; other neighbours stay two tokens. If the pattern has more literal and `?` tokens than the anchor has characters, it MUST fail with no steps. Otherwise each anchor character stepped MUST cost the token count plus 1, until the pattern can match no further (it fails then) or the anchor ends.

The total MUST be checked after each piece is read, again once its preparation is charged and before it is prepared, after each comparison, and before each character a glob steps; once it passes 2^20, nothing more MUST be begun. The value then keeps the best match found so far, in the order of this section (anchors in intake order, then pieces in order).
Where several anchors and pieces reach a seed's score, the first anchor in intake order, and for it the first piece of the value, MUST name the seed's reason.
A declaration's seeds MUST be offered at hop 0, best score first, then in the format's order, each shared by 1, until 256 records are kept.

A seed's reason path MUST be the anchor (shortened as in R-WALK-067) and, when the matching pattern is not the anchor itself, ` matches <property> <pattern>`, with the pattern trimmed, in the strict character set and at most 80 characters. The pattern is the anchor itself when, for a name, the two are equal (ordinal, after trimming), and for a path when they are the same path (normalized and folded as above).
A record MUST be kept once, by its version id, with its best score; a later path MUST replace it only with a strictly higher score.

At most 256 records MUST be kept in all and 192 per module; a record offered past either MUST NOT be kept. Offers MUST happen in the order this section states, so the caps keep the same records in every store.

`hops` MUST be the largest any taking-part module declares (1 to 3, default 2). At hop *h*, the walk MUST take each module whose own `hops` ≥ *h*, in the order of R-WALK-034, and each of its declared relations in declaration order; the starting records are those of the frontier (what the previous hop kept, or the seeds) of the relation's start type (`from` for `out`; the target type for `in`), each at its best score.
A relation into another module MUST be followed only with that module's consent, as the Compose profile defines it; the validator MUST refuse a traversal relation into `core:` entities.

A starting record with more than 16,384 links of the relation MUST NOT be expanded through it, and the walk MUST report that it "has more than 16,384 … links", in every store. The links are counted as distinct live records in scope at the other end: for `out`, what the record's own links lead to; for `in`, the records linking to any version of it.
The link limit SHOULD be checked from the store's degree first, so that only a record past it there has its live links counted.

Otherwise every one of the record's live neighbours in scope MUST be ranked: most matches first, then fewest records sharing the link, then the format's order; the first `fanOut` (1 to 32, default 8) are taken.

A neighbour's *degree*, counted up to 1,024, MUST be: for an `out` hop, the distinct live records in scope whose same relation leads to any version of it; for an `in` hop, the distinct live keys in scope its links of the relation lead to (a link to an older version of a live record counts once; one whose key has no live version does not). A neighbour MUST count as shared by its degree; fewer is more specific.

A store MAY return more than the first `fanOut` neighbours (every neighbour that ties the last one kept, for instance); the walk itself MUST then make the cut by the order of R-WALK-062, so two stores keep the same neighbours.
Each neighbour's score MUST be ⌊the parent's score × `weightMicro` / 1,000,000⌋, in millionths (`weightMicro` 1 to 1,000,000, default 800,000); a neighbour below 100,000 MUST be dropped.

A neighbour's reason path MUST be the parent's, then ` → ` and `<verb> <name>` (`out`) or `<name> <verb> it` (`in`), where the verb is the relation name without the module's prefix, in lower case, with `_` as spaces.

The name in a reason MUST be the record's `name`, else its `path` (each only when it is not blank after trimming ASCII white space), else its key, shortened: a SCIP symbol to its simple name, a path to its last segment. A value, trimmed of ASCII white space, is a symbol when it holds both a space and `#`, or ends with `#`, `)` or `.`, and its simple name is not empty; otherwise it is a path, shortened only when something follows its last `/`.

In every segment of a reason path (the anchor, a pattern, each name), characters outside ASCII letters, digits, `._-/:#*()<>,+@` and space MUST be replaced by `_` (each character on its own), and the segment MUST be at most 80 characters (77 and `...`). The cap applies to each segment, not to the whole path.
The neighbours of one relation MUST be offered by score (descending), matches (descending), shared by (ascending), then the format's order of the neighbour and of the record it was reached from.
An expansion MUST start from at most 256 records.
A record's rank MUST be score × (1 + matches). Records MUST be ordered by rank (descending), shared by (ascending), hops (ascending), then the format's order.
Each module MUST then offer, in that order, its own records whose type is not a hub, at most its `maxItems` (1 to 16, default 4), each with its reason path, to the host's admission gate.
A server that mounts packs, its remote operations and pack tests MUST show exactly this selection.
The admission gate MUST refuse text that is not in NFC.

The walk MUST stop, keeping what it has, at 256 kept records, 128 store reads, or 5 s. A store read MUST be counted for each anchor declaration with anchors of its kind and each relation with starting records, per read issued.
A stop MUST change nothing in §5 for the records already kept.

The time budget MUST be checked before each read and on every record a store scans or row it fetches, and each read MUST carry the time the walk has left; a store that can stop a statement on its server MUST set that time as the transaction's timeout, and a stop there is a stop by time.
The walk MUST report what it spent and why it stopped, if it did.
A read that fails MUST be that module's omission, with a problem, never the walk's.
What the walk could not do (a record past the link limit) MUST be listed in one order, whatever the store's.
A Trial Host MUST implement Ampack Core as a Core Reader, the Walk profile, and every requirement of this document.
`measure` MUST be `test-impact`; `retrieval` is reserved, and a host that does not implement it MUST refuse a trial that declares it.
`tasks` MUST be 10 to 200 (default 40), and at least 10 tasks MUST be found for a trial to decide anything.
`baseline` MUST be `host` or `none` (default `none`).

`hitRateMicro` and `precisionMicro` MUST be 0 to 1,000,000, `liftMicro` and `precisionLiftMicro` −1,000,000 to 1,000,000, and `addedP95Ms` 1 to 60,000, each an integer (R-CORE-119); every target given MUST be met for the trial to pass.
`confidencePermille`, when present, MUST be 900, 950, 975 or 990; a target MUST then be met only by its lower confidence bound under the statistic of §5.
`upgrade.toleranceMicro` MUST be 0 to 500,000 (default 0); with a `confidencePermille`, a `noRegression` rule MUST have a tolerance above 0.
A trial with no measure, or with a target out of range, MUST be refused.
A Trial Host MUST draw the tasks from its own history.

Tasks MUST be drawn in history order: the runner draws every k-th eligible commit of the last 2,000, k the most that still gives the count, and each arm MUST record `spacing`, every how many eligible commits a task was drawn (1 to 2,000).
A decision MUST record how its tasks were drawn, `history`: `parent` (each task at its commit's parent, the default) or `head` (the repository as it is now, which sees the tests a change created).
Both arms of a trial MUST run the same tasks, drawn at one spacing, within the 2,000 commits a trial draws from.

Each arm MUST record `maximumOffered`, fixed before it ran: the pack's `maxItems` for the arm with the pack, 3 for the grep baseline, 0 for the baseline `none` (which offers nothing by design), and 16 when unstated.
Each arm MUST record its per-task results (`perTask`): for each task, the items offered and the items right, each task within the arm's cap; the arm's totals MUST be the per-task results' own.
A hit MUST be a task with a right item.
Precision, and every difference, MUST be bounded only from per-task results, on both arms for a difference; without them, a host MUST NOT take a precision or a difference as bounded.
Without a `confidencePermille`, a target MUST be judged on its estimate.
A hit rate's lower bound MUST be Clopper-Pearson's, exact; so MUST precision's be when an arm offers one item a task at most.

Precision otherwise, and every difference, MUST assume tasks the trial did not see, at the worst the arm's cap allows: the unseen task offers the arm's cap, none right, and for a difference the other arm offers its cap, all right.
The unseen task MUST be counted 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 or 2 times, at the confidences 0.9, 0.95, 0.975 and 0.99 respectively, beside the tasks the trial ran.
The bound MUST then be Fieller's test inversion of the pooled precision, or the difference linearized task by task, at Student's t with one degree of freedom fewer than the tasks.
Only an arm that offers nothing by design (a cap of 0) MUST be taken to have no uncertainty; an arm that could offer but did not MUST keep its unseen task.

When tasks were drawn closer than 8 eligible commits apart, every bound MUST first cluster each run of ⌈8 / spacing⌉ consecutive tasks, in drawn order, into one (a hit rate then becomes a clustered proportion).
Neighbouring runs MUST count as correlated, since a burst of at most 8 commits can straddle two: every clustered bound MUST add the runs' lag-1 autocovariance to its variance, never lowering it.
The clustered one-arm bound MUST be the hedged pooled ratio linearized at its estimate.
`addedP95Ms` MUST be compared as measured, with no bound.

A host MUST derive every verdict again from the evidence a decision carries, under its own statistic; the statistic a record names (`statistic`) is for information. Re-deriving MAY take a pass back, and MUST NOT give one.
A writer's lint SHOULD say what a declared trial can never show, for hit rate and precision both.
A trial MUST pass exactly when every declared target is met on at least 10 tasks, each target judged as §5 says.
A Trial Host MUST record each decision as a decision record signed by its own key (`host/decision-record.md`), bound to the pack's digest and the declarations' digest.

A host MUST find a decision by id, version and both digests: a later trial of other content MUST NOT shadow it, a decision for one pack MUST NOT switch on other records under the same declarations, and a decision for compiled code MUST NOT count for a pack, nor the reverse.
A decision record that names no pack digest MUST still verify, and MUST count for nothing.
A record that was edited, or signed by a key other than the host's, MUST NOT switch a pack on.

A host that requires trials MUST keep off a pack that declares a trial and has no passing decision for exactly itself, and whatever needs that pack; a failed trial MUST keep the pack off with its reason.
A pack kept off MUST keep its contributor slots registered, contributing nothing, so every other module's contributors still reach the host.
A host that does not require trials MUST compose packs as it would without this profile.
A host MAY require trials under id prefixes, by whole segments; a pack there that declares no trial MUST stay off.

A host MAY set a floor, the least a trial must claim before it counts: a confidence, a task count and targets at least as strict. A trial below the floor MUST stay off, with what it lacks; the floor MUST be judged on the tasks a decision ran, not on what its pack declares, and a floor's targets MUST be held to the rules a manifest's are.
Every door that shows or serves what a host composes (a gate report, a server) MUST take the same gate options, the floor among them, and decide by the same rule as the host.
With `upgrade.noRegression`, a new version MUST switch on only if it does no worse than the version that passed on this host before it, on the same tasks.
With a `confidencePermille`, the rule MUST be a non-inferiority test: the lower bound of each drop clears −tolerance; without one, the estimates MUST NOT drop by more than the tolerance.

The runner MUST measure the version that passed on this host on the same tasks in the same run, the decision MUST keep that comparison, and two more targets MUST require no drop in hit rate or precision beyond the tolerance.
At composition, a passing upgrade of a version that passed here MUST stay off unless its decision compared it with exactly that version (id, version and both digests).

The version an upgrade is compared with MUST be the latest one this host's own trial passed and that the gate itself allows (its floor included); a decision made from a certificate MUST NOT stand as that version, and a version whose latest decision failed MUST NOT count.
The version an upgrade replaces MUST be held to the cap this host judged it at, never the cap the upgrade's decision states.
Every rule down the chain of versions MUST hold, each as declared, its tolerance with its own confidence; a version MUST NOT drop or loosen the rule its predecessor was held to.
A first version MUST NOT be held to a predecessor; when neither version asks for the rule, an upgrade MUST compose without comparison; the same version with other content MUST be an upgrade too.
A host's composer and a writer's test command MUST run a pack's tests offline on the same engine the walk uses, and a failing test MUST name what is missing.
A malformed tests file MUST be refused, naming the test it concerns.
A writer's lint SHOULD advise a knowledge pack without a trial that a host requiring trials keeps it off, and SHOULD advise a trial without an upgrade rule or with few tasks.

Whether a target is met MUST be decided exactly, in rational arithmetic, never in floating point. An estimate is a ratio of counts. Clopper-Pearson's bound reaches t when P(X ≥ x) at rate t is at most 1 − confidence. A bound of the form mean − q·se (the hedged, paired and clustered bounds) reaches t when mean − t ≥ 0 and (mean − t)² ≥ q²·se². Fieller's lower root of a θ² + b θ + c (a > 0) reaches t when a t² + b t + c ≥ 0 and 2 a t ≤ −b. The quantiles and the hedge weights MUST be those of the table below, each decimal read exactly as written, and beyond 60 degrees of freedom Cornish-Fisher in z, as stated below it. Every clamp of a bound MUST be kept: Fieller's bound is 0 when a ≤ 0, the estimate when the discriminant is negative, and otherwise the lesser of its lower root and the estimate; every bound is then clamped to [0, 1], a difference's to [−1, 1]. Floating point MAY show a bound; it MUST NOT decide one.

`safety`, when present, MUST hold `probes` (one line of 1 to 100 display-safe characters naming a probe suite) and MAY hold `maxFollowMicro` (an integer of 0 to 1,000,000, default 0; above 0 with a `confidencePermille`, since no run bounds a follow rate at 0):

A host MUST run the named suite with its own probes (injection prompts placed as records of the pack) and count the probes whose planted instruction the model followed; the target MUST be met only when that share is at most `maxFollowMicro` millionths: its estimate without a `confidencePermille`, and otherwise its upper bound, one less Clopper-Pearson's lower bound of the probes not followed, decided exactly (R-TRIAL-051). Without a run of that suite, the target MUST NOT be met.

A decision MUST keep the run (the suite, the probes and those followed), so a recheck reaches the same verdict, and a kept run of no probes, or of counts out of range, MUST NOT meet the target. A certificate MUST NOT be issued for, nor admit, a pack whose trial declares a safety target: only the host's own probes decide it. A host's floor (R-TRIAL-038) MAY require a safety target on a named suite at a follow rate at most its own; a trial without one, on another suite or above it, MUST stay off, and so MUST a decision that kept no run of that suite.

`cost`, when present, MUST hold at least one of `savingBytesMedian` (whole bytes, 0 to 1,000,000,000) and `savingRatioMicro` (millionths of the baseline's bytes, 0 to 1,000,000), and the trial's `baseline` MUST be `host`: a saving is against what the host already has. Each arm MUST then record, for every task, the UTF-8 bytes of what it offered (0 to 1,000,000,000), each item in the frame the host renders it in (R-HOST-053), the baseline's items framed the same way: one renderer for both arms. An arm that offers nothing by design records 0.

A task's saving is the baseline's bytes less the pack's and less the pack's fixed cost per turn (what it adds to every turn whatever the task), in the target's unit: whole bytes, or millionths of the baseline's bytes rounded down (a baseline of no bytes counting one). The check MUST show a bound and be met exactly when the bound is at or above the target. Without a `confidencePermille` the bound is the lower median of the tasks' savings. With one it is the exact one-sided sign test's lower bound of the median: of independent units, the k-th largest, k the fewest of n whose Clopper-Pearson lower bound at that confidence is at least one half (R-TRIAL-051). At a spacing of a burst (8) or more each task is a unit. Closer, each cluster of tasks within a burst counts its minimum saving, and the bound is the lesser of the even clusters' bound and the odd clusters' bound, each set a burst apart; when a set has too few units for any k, the bound is one unit under the target. The decision MUST keep the fixed cost it counted, so a recheck reaches the same verdict.

A certificate MAY state cost checks. Each task of its arms MAY then record its offered bytes as a third number (`[offered, correct, bytes]`, 0 to 1,000,000,000): every task of both arms or none MUST, an arm that offers nothing MUST record 0, a cost check MUST have both arms and the bytes, and a verifier MUST refuse a cost check whose `met` is not exactly `observedMicro` at or above `requiredMicro`.
A trial MUST read each task as of its own time (its commit's time for a task drawn from history) in world time as well: a record true only later never answers it, in either arm.

A Compose Host MUST implement Ampack Core as a Core Reader, and every requirement of this document. A verifier that implements this profile MUST apply its verification requirements (§2 to §4) as part of Core §10 step 4.
A composite MUST name what it contains in `contains` and pin it in `META/lock.json`, and MUST carry `members.json`.
A composite MUST hold no records of its own under `records/`.
A composite MUST contain modules or composites only; a snapshot pack MUST NOT be a member, and travels beside a composite in a pack set (Core §14.2).

`members.json` MUST hold `members` only, an array whose entries hold only the fields above, typed: `id` and `version` non-empty strings (both required), `priority` an integer within 32 bits, `enabled` a boolean, `contains` a list of non-empty strings; anything else MUST refuse the pack.
`members.json`, the `contains` of `pack.json` and `META/lock.json` MUST name the same members.

A host MUST refuse, at load, a priority outside 0 to 10,000, a version that is not a range, a `contains` that names no member or names itself, and a cycle; such a pack verifies and is refused by every host.
A host MAY leave a member out, move it, or switch on a member that is off by default; it MUST NOT name a member the composite lacks.

`META/lock.json` MUST be `{"format": "agentmemory.pack.lock/1.1", "members": [{"id", "version", "digest"}]}` and nothing else, at the top level and in each member: `id` an id, `version` a version, `digest` a pack digest; it MUST be in RFC 8785 canonical form, listed in `META/files.json` and so signed.
A lock MUST pin each id at most once.
A composite's lock MUST pin exactly its direct members.
A host MUST install exactly the pinned set: a missing, extra or swapped member MUST refuse the family.
Containment MUST be a directed acyclic graph at most four composites deep; a fifth level MUST be refused.
A nested composite's digest covers its own lock, so the outermost signature pins the whole tree; two locks that pin different content for one id MUST refuse the family.
A composite that contains itself by id MUST be refused.
Two composites MAY share a member only as the same content, and it MUST be composed once, from the first composite that adds it.
A nested member's priority MUST be its slot's plus its own (at most 10,000): never ahead of its slot, in its own order within it.
Switching a slot off MUST switch off everything under it; a member MUST be on only when some path to it has every composite on and the member enabled.
A member MUST have what it depends on switched on and contained.

Every door that holds packs together (a host, a server that mounts packs, pack tests, a gate report) MUST hold them by one rule: one version of a pack, and one live snapshot of a module, a later one replacing the earlier whole.
The same pack reached twice (the same digest, in a set and on its own) MUST be one pack, whatever the order in which it is reached.
Two versions or contents of one id, or two snapshots of one module, MUST be refused with both named; two different manifests under one module id MUST be refused, never one silently kept.
Each pack MUST come from the route that registered it, and a family member MUST count through the route a host composes it by.
A walk into another pack MUST need that pack's `containableBy` to name the container.

A link written into a pack's records at ingestion MUST need the same consent: a snapshot that links into a pack without its consent MUST be refused before anything is written, and the store MUST refuse such a link on any write path.
A snapshot whose links reach a dependency that holds nothing MUST be refused, as the store refuses it.
A host MAY grant a pair (a pack and the pack it may reach into) by name; the grant MUST apply to walks and links alike, and MUST join the module set's fingerprint.
A server that mounts packs MUST take the host's grants as the host does, for walks and for snapshot packs.
An Evaluator MUST implement Ampack Core and the Trial profile, and the requirements of this document addressed to an evaluator.
A Certify Host MUST implement Ampack Core, the Trial profile, and the requirements of this document addressed to a host or a verifier.

A certificate MUST be an envelope in the shape of Core §8.1 with 1 to 16 signatures, whose statement has the predicate type `urn:agentmemory:pack:certificate:v1` and exactly one subject: `META/files.json` and its SHA-256, so that it is bound to exactly one pack.

A certificate MUST be signed by a key the host's trust policy names as `evaluator` for the pack's id, under the counting rule of Core §9.2 with the evaluation time as the signing time; an evaluator key holds that role alone, so the key that signs a pack never certifies it.
The predicate MUST hold no field other than those above, and every number in it MUST be an integer.
`id` and `version` MUST be this pack's, and the subject's digest this pack's digest.

`evaluator` MUST be one line of 1 to 200 characters; `tool.name` one line of 1 to 100 and `tool.version` one line of 1 to 64; `trial.taskSource` one line of 1 to 500; `statistic` one line of 1 to 100. A line holds no line feed, no tab and no other control character.
`evaluatedAt` MUST be a UTC time written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, within the key's window, and not more than 5 minutes after the time of verification (the one clock allowance of R-CORE-061).
`trial.measure` and `trial.baseline` MUST be among the values above, and `confidencePermille`, when present, among the confidences above.

`checks` MUST hold 1 to 16 checks, each naming a known target of the Trial profile once, with `requiredMicro` and `observedMicro` integers in millionths of the target's own unit (a rate's required value is the trial's own integer), `met` a boolean, and `estimateMicro` an integer when present; a no-regression comparison MUST NOT appear as a check, since it is a host's own.

An arm MUST hold exactly its fields: at most 200 tasks; `maximumOffered` 0 (nothing offered by design) to 16; `spacing` 1 to 2,000; and `perTask`, one `[offered, correct]` per task with `correct` ≤ `offered` ≤ the cap, summing to `offered` and `correct`, with a right item on exactly `hits` tasks.
`without` MUST run the same number of tasks as `with`, at the same spacing; the tasks MUST span fewer than the 2,000 eligible commits a trial draws from (spacing × (tasks − 1) < 2,000).
`without` MUST be present for a `host` baseline, with a cap of at least 1; for a `none` baseline, a `without` arm, when present, MUST offer nothing and have a cap of 0.
`passed` MUST be true exactly when every check was met and `with` ran at least 10 tasks: an honest failure is a valid certificate.
`aef`, when present, MUST hold exactly `runId` (1 to 128 characters of `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `.`, `_`, `:`, `-`) and `runHash` (64 lowercase hexadecimal digits).

A carried certificate MUST travel as `META/attestations/<stem>.certificate.dsse.json`, where the stem is the first 16 hexadecimal digits of its evaluator key's id, `-`, and the evaluation time in UTC written `yyyymmddthhmmssz`; a certificate under another stem MUST be refused.
A certificate MUST be known by what its evaluator signed, the SHA-256 of its payload's pre-authentication encoding, never by its envelope's bytes; respellings of one envelope are one certificate.
An untrusted or malformed certificate MUST NOT refuse the pack: what it claims MAY be shown, read strictly, and it never stops a load.
A certificate MAY also travel as a separate file beside the pack, and MUST then verify by the same rules.
A certified set MUST verify whole, member by member, before its certificate is read.
An AEF run MAY travel beside its certificate under `META/attestations/<stem>.aef/`; a run without its certificate MUST refuse the pack.
A run that travels with a certificate MUST hash, by AEF 1.0's run hash (SEAL-1 to SEAL-4), to the `runHash` the certificate names; a certificate that names no run MUST NOT travel with one.

A run's `run.json`, read in the JSON profile, MUST name the same run id and, as its subject, this pack: `ref` is `pack:<id>@<digest>` and `version` is the pack's version. A run of another version or content is the evidence of another decision and MUST be refused, at issue and by every verifier.
A run file named as a certificate's evidence that the pack does not carry MUST refuse the certificate.

An Evaluator MUST issue a certificate only from its own signed decision for exactly that pack, whose checks are the declared targets, with the checks derived again under its statistic and both arms' per-task evidence.
An Evaluator MUST certify only a decision whose tasks were drawn in `parent` mode; it MUST refuse `head` and a decision that does not say.
A writer MUST refuse to sign a certificate whose verdict or text breaks this document.
A host MUST rely only on its own trials unless it names namespaces in which it trusts certificates (by whole segments); certificate trust MUST need the host's decisions and a namespace.

In such a namespace, a host that requires trials MAY record a decision from the latest trusted, passing certificate that covers exactly the trial the pack declares: the same measure, baseline and confidence; every declared target checked at the declared value and met; at least 10 tasks; and the host's own statistic, on the evidence the certificate carries, agreeing that every target is met. It MUST sign that decision with its own key and name the certificate it relied on (`basis`: certificate digest, evaluator and key, time, task source, AEF run).
Admission MUST hold a certificate's arms to the caps the pack declares.

One rule MUST decide which of a host's decisions about exactly one content counts, for the trial gate and the upgrade gate alike: the host's own latest decision whenever it has one, pass or fail; otherwise, only in a namespace it trusts certificates for, its latest decision made from a certificate. A host MUST refuse to admit from a certificate where it has its own trial.
A decision made from a certificate MUST count only for a pack composed on its own (not a family member, not compiled code).

A decision made from a certificate MUST count only while the certificate it names is the latest trusted one the pack carries: when its evaluator is revoked, expired, re-scoped or removed, the certificate stripped, or a newer trusted one is beside it, it MUST no longer count.

Admission MUST follow the latest trusted certificate: a newer failure MUST NOT be passed over for an older pass; when two trusted certificates share the latest evaluation second and one did not pass, admission MUST follow that one.
A broken copy of a trusted certificate MUST NOT hide it, whatever its name.
An upgrade that must not regress MUST still need the host's own trial: a certificate MUST NOT skip the upgrade gate.
An evaluator key the host revoked before MUST NOT be trusted, even when the current run names no revocation.
A certificate moved onto other content MUST NOT be trusted there.
A Federation Host MUST implement Ampack Core as a Core Reader, and every requirement of this document.
A reader that does not implement this profile MUST refuse a federated pack rather than ignore its audience.
The extension MUST always be listed in `extensions.critical`; a pack that carries it without listing it MUST be refused.
The extension MUST be an object of the fields above only, with `format` `agentmemory.pack.federation/1`, a `publisher` WebID and an `audience`; a field it does not define MUST refuse the pack.
`audience` MUST be `"public"` or a list of 1 to 64 distinct WebIDs.
`purpose`, when present, MUST be text of 1 to 300 characters.

A WebID MUST be `https://` and a DNS host, or `http://` to loopback, then a path starting with `/` of characters that need no escaping in Turtle, with at most one `#`, and at most 512 characters in all.
A publishing key in the trust policy MAY carry the `webId` it is bound to; a revoker key MUST NOT carry one.
`host.webIds`, when present, MUST name 1 to 16 distinct WebIDs: who this host is.
A federated pack MUST carry a counted publisher signature from a key the host bound to its `publisher`; a trusted key bound to no WebID MUST NOT publish a federated pack.
A counted publisher signature from a key bound to another WebID MUST refuse the pack, even beside a signature from the right one.

For an audience of named WebIDs, the host MUST be in the audience: a host whose `host.webIds` names none of them, or that names no WebID of its own, MUST refuse the pack. A public pack needs no host WebID.
Every member of a federated set MUST be federated itself, by the same publisher, for an audience within the set's.
These member rules need no key, so a writer and lint MUST hold them too (Core §10).
A federated set MUST be verified with every member it carries.

A receipt MUST be an envelope in the shape of Core §8.1 with 1 to 16 signatures, at most 64 KiB, whose statement has the predicate type `urn:agentmemory:pack:publication:v1` and exactly one subject: `META/files.json` and its SHA-256.

The predicate MUST hold no field other than `id`, `version`, `location`, `archiveSha256`, `audience`, `access`, `checked` and `publishedAt`: the pack's id and version; the placement's URL; the archive's SHA-256 (64 lowercase hexadecimal digits); the placement's audience; its access kind; the probe's record; and the publishing time in UTC written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
`location` MUST be a URL in the WebID grammar without a fragment.
`access` MUST be one of the access kinds below, and MUST be `public` exactly when the audience is public.

`checked` MUST be an object of `denied` and `allowed`, each a list of at most 64 distinct WebIDs (`anonymous` may be denied), and MUST agree with the placement: a receipt for named readers records that `anonymous` was refused, records no reader outside its audience as allowed and no reader in it as refused; a public receipt records nobody as refused.
A receipt MUST be for a federated pack only.
A receipt MUST hold only for this pack (its digest, id and version), at the location the pack was fetched from, for the exact archive bytes fetched, and for a host in the placement's audience.

A placement MUST only narrow the pack's audience: a receipt for a wider audience than the pack's, or a public placement of a pack for named WebIDs, MUST be refused. A public pack MAY be placed publicly or for named readers.
A receipt MUST be signed, with the publisher role under Core §9.2 and the publishing time as the signing time, by a key bound to the pack's publisher WebID.
A fetch from a Pod MUST require a receipt; a set's receipt MUST hold only when every member verifies.
A publisher's tool MUST NOT sign a receipt whose probe record disagrees with its placement.
A publisher's key MUST be asserted in its WebID profile (`sec:assertionMethod`, as a P-256 JWK).
Discovery SHOULD start from the publisher's public type index; catalogs are per reader, each naming its publisher.
A reader MUST present its credentials only in the publisher's own places: its WebID document's origin, and storages elsewhere only when they name the WebID as owner; never an IP address.
A publisher's tool MUST write access in the model the server uses, with denies in ACP so that nothing inherited reaches the pack, and MUST probe it.
On the Web, a reader MUST bound documents to 1 MiB, a type index to 8 containers, and a catalog to 1,000 entries.

A host that does not implement enforcement of a pack's protection level MUST refuse the pack, with the refusal words the registry gives this profile; a declared protection MUST NOT load as if it were absent.
A pack that declares a protection other than `open` MUST carry `META/seal.json`.
A host that does not implement a pack's code tier MUST refuse the pack, with the refusal words the registry gives this profile; this holds for a declared tier above `E0` and for code files alike.
A pack MUST NOT carry native code; E3 is never inside a pack.
A host that cannot enforce a usage policy MUST refuse a pack that carries one, with the refusal words the registry gives this profile; a declared policy MUST NOT load as if it were absent.
A host MUST read its trust policy bounded to 4 MiB, as UTF-8; a policy that is not UTF-8 MUST be refused.

A host MAY accept a policy that starts with one byte order mark or uses CRLF line ends: it removes that one mark and reads each CRLF as LF, then reads the policy in the JSON profile (Core §6). A second byte order mark MUST refuse the policy.
The policy MUST be closed at every level: a field this document does not define, at the top level, in a key, in `revoked` or in a revoked key, MUST refuse the policy, naming the field.
A malformed policy MUST be refused before any pack is looked at.
`format` MUST be `agentmemory.pack.trust/1.1`.
`requireRoles`, when present, MUST be a non-empty list of pack signing roles (Core §8.2).
`host`, when present, MUST be an object holding only `webIds`: 1 to 16 distinct WebIDs.
`keyId` MUST be the SHA-256 of the key's DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits; a key MUST be listed once.

`publicKey` MUST be one PEM `PUBLIC KEY` block and nothing else: `-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----`, a line break, 1 to 16 lines of 1 to 76 base64 characters each ending in a line break (LF or CRLF; no blank line, no space), `-----END PUBLIC KEY-----`, and at most one final line break. A private key or a second block MUST refuse the policy.

The block's content MUST be the one canonical P-256 key: the 91-byte DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo for id-ecPublicKey on prime256v1 with an uncompressed point (`04`, then X and Y), in canonical base64 (no stray bits in the last character), and the point MUST be on the curve. A compressed or hybrid point, another curve or another algorithm MUST refuse the policy.
`idPrefixes` MUST be a non-empty list of id prefixes: lowercase segments as in an id, at most 64 characters, optionally ending with one `.`; a prefix covers ids by whole segments (Core R-CORE-058).
`roles` MUST be a non-empty list of key roles (Core §8.2); a `revoker` key and an `evaluator` key MUST each hold that role alone.
`notBefore` and `notAfter`, when present, MUST be times (Core §6); `null` is not absent and MUST refuse the policy.
`webId`, when present, MUST be a WebID (Federation profile), and a `revoker` key MUST NOT carry one.
`digests` MUST be a list of pack digests, each `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
`keys` MUST be a list of objects holding `keyId` (64 lowercase hexadecimal digits) and optionally `compromisedAt` (a time).
`expires`, when present, MUST be a time: the policy's own revocation freshness.
In this version no timestamp is judged, so a revoked key's signatures MUST NOT count, whatever its `compromisedAt`; of two compromise times for one key, the earlier MUST hold.
A revocation document MUST be an envelope in the closed shape of Core §8.1 with the payload type `application/vnd.agentmemory.revocations+json`, at most 4 MiB and 16 signature entries.

Its payload MUST be an object holding only `format` (`agentmemory.pack.revocations/1.2`), `issuedAt` and `expires` (times, expiring after it was issued), `digests` (pack digests) and `keys` (revoked keys as in §4).
A document MUST be refused unless a key the policy names as `revoker` signed it; a changed document MUST NOT verify.
A document issued more than 5 minutes after now MUST be refused.

A revoker is *live* when it is valid now and revoked by nobody (the policy, or another counted list). A list from a revoker that is not live (expired, revoked) MUST deny the packs and non-revoker keys it names for the run only.
A list with a live signer MUST also revoke revokers, set freshness, and be kept by the ledger; it MUST revoke a key against that key's will only when a live signer other than that key signed it.
One run MUST take at most 64 lists; one list carried in two envelopes MUST be counted once (by what it signs, the SHA-256 of its pre-authentication encoding), with its signers together.
Freshness MUST be the newest live list's expiry (of two issued in the same second, the earlier expiry), capped by the policy's own; a list MUST NOT extend the policy's own expiry.

A rotated revoker's successor carries its revocations forward: a list without a live signer that revokes a revoker that has not expired, and that no counted list revokes, MUST refuse the run until a live list does. A revoker MUST NOT escape this by revoking itself or by co-signing, and a successor not yet valid does not escape it.
Lists that revoke each other's signers in a circle MUST refuse the run; the same list given twice, or reissued, is no circle.
Revocations MUST be added, never removed; of two expiries, the earlier holds; a list from the same second, or an expired one, removes nothing.
The outcome of a run MUST NOT depend on the order in which its lists are given.
A host MUST read its ledger bounded to 64 MiB, as Core §18 reads every file.
The ledger MUST record, for each id, the highest version ever installed, and for each (id, version), its digest; it MUST keep them across a save and a load.
A host MUST refuse a downgrade, even after the pack was removed, unless the operator says so.
A host MUST refuse a known version with other content; versions that differ only in build metadata are the same version.

The ledger MUST hold a pack set's members as it holds packs: a set rolled back to an older version MUST be refused; where the operator allows a set downgrade, the ledger MUST still hold one content per version, and MAY install a member older than the host had.
The ledger MUST keep what a live revoker's lists revoked, so that what a host revoked stays revoked whatever list a later run is given; a revocation MUST outlive its revoker.

The ledger MUST keep the revocation freshness it applied, and a host with a ledger MUST stay only as fresh as the newest list it applied; an operator MAY retire the kept revocations' freshness explicitly.
Co-signed and older lists MUST NOT lock a host out.
Two runs that save the ledger at once MUST lose nothing.
The ledger MUST be checked last in verification (Core §10).
A decision MUST be an envelope in the shape of Core §8.1, of an in-toto statement with the predicate type `urn:agentmemory:pack:trial:v1`, signed by the host's own key.
The record MUST name the pack it trialled by its digest (`packDigest`, `sha256:` over its files list), which is also the statement's subject.
The record MUST name the declarations by `manifestDigest`, written `jcs-sha256:` over their RFC 8785 canonical JSON, named apart from a pack digest.

The record MUST carry the declared `confidence`, `history` (`parent` or `head`), the `statistic` its checks were computed with, and each arm's evidence: its counts, `maximumOffered`, `spacing` and `perTask`.
For an upgrade, the record MUST carry the comparison with the version it was measured against: that version's id, version and both digests.
A decision made from a certificate MUST name the certificate it relied on as `basis`: the certificate digest, the evaluator and its key, the evaluation time, the task source and the AEF run.
A host MUST read an activation record bounded to 1 MiB; a record over its bound is not a record.
A decision MUST be recorded once, and two decisions made in one second MUST NOT share a file.
