The declarations' digest MUST be stable: the same declarations MUST give the same `manifestDigest` on every host.
A type's name MUST begin with the module's `labelPrefix` and a relation's with its upper-snake form, except built-in types and relations, which are named in the pack by their built-in names.

A built-in type MUST be stored as the prefix and the type's name in PascalCase (`note` as `<Prefix>Note`), a built-in relation as the prefix's upper-snake form and the relation's (`part_of` as `<PREFIX>_PART_OF`), with `shared` scope; a record's `type` and a link's `relation` MUST be mapped the same way as the record is read. A host that writes such records into a pack MUST write their built-in names, and never its own binding (the `builtIn` member it keeps on them).

A pack that uses built-in types and declares no `ontology.json` MUST be given the prefix of its id's last segment in PascalCase (`com.example.lantern-notes` as `LanternNotes`); when that prefix is another module's, the pack MUST be refused, as any prefix two modules claim is; its author then declares a `labelPrefix` in `ontology.json`.

A host that renders a module's items into a model's context MUST put every one inside a frame, never as bare text, on every path that renders them: an element `record` whose attributes are, for a record a pack brought, `pack` (the pack's id), `version` (the pack's version), `type` and `key`, and, for any other module item, `module`, its version, and its `type` and `key` when it has them; then the item's text, then the closing tag. Whether an item is framed MUST NOT depend on it naming its pack: one that has lost its source is framed with its module. The frames of one section MUST stand inside the section's one `recalled_memory` element, which names its category. A host that returns records as structured data, each with its pack, type and key as separate fields (AgentMemory's coding MCP host, `ampack serve`), meets this by those fields; the client that puts them into a prompt frames them.
Inside a frame, `<` and `>` MUST be written `<` and `>`, and inside an attribute the double quote too (`"`), so no text can close its frame, open another, or change what a header says.
A frame MUST be applied whatever the pack's trust, its tier or the host's admission decision: a record the admission lets through is framed; one it refuses is left out.

Every record's text MUST pass the host's admission of untrusted content before it is framed into a model's context (in AgentMemory, `IMemoryContextAdmissionPolicy`, which refuses or flags instruction-like text under the host's security mode).

A writer's lint MUST report every high-severity finding of its content scan (a secret, a payment card or account number, an injection payload) as an error when asked to (`--safety`), and always for a pack of the `curated` or `premium` tier.

A store MUST keep a pack record's effective life (R-CORE-128 to 130) as its instants, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `expires_at` and `review_by`, and a changed life MUST be a new version of the record, never left as it was. Every view and walk MUST offer only the records live at the request's valid time (`AsOf`), or the host's now when it names none, by one definition of liveness, applied where records leave the store, before any limit, anchor match or fan-out cut counts them, and again where the walk seeds, steers and offers. A history view lists versions and is not filtered.

A valid-time pin alone reads the store's current knowledge as of that world time: what the host now holds true then, including records it learned later; a record without a life is true at every time. To read what the host held then, a request names its transaction time too (`SystemAsOf`), which views read and a walk refuses. Core memory recall reads both clocks at the pin; module records keep their own lives, so the two may differ, by design.

An embeddings set MUST be two files, `embeddings/<name>.st` and `embeddings/<name>.json`, its name 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits or `-`, beginning with a letter or digit; every file under `embeddings/` MUST belong to a set, and a pack MUST carry at most 8 sets.
`embeddings/<name>.json` MUST be in the JSON profile, hold only these fields, each of them but `modelDigest`, and name `format` `ampack.embeddings/1`:

`model` MUST be one line of 1 to 200 characters, and `modelDigest`, when present, one line of 1 to 200; `dtype` MUST be one of these, `dimension` an integer of 1 to 4,096, `normalized` a boolean, and `distance` one of these:

`rows` MUST list 1 to 5,000 rows, each `[type, key]` (two strings) naming a record the pack holds, each record at most once. A record line names a record when its `type` and `key` are both strings; the set is checked once every record line has passed the JSON profile.

`embeddings/<name>.st` MUST be in the safetensors layout: an 8-byte little-endian header length of 1 to 65,536, a header of that length in the JSON profile, a JSON object from its first byte to its last but trailing spaces, then the data, and nothing after it.

The header MUST hold exactly one tensor, `vectors`, and no other member (`__metadata__` included), of exactly `dtype`, `shape` and `data_offsets`; its `dtype` MUST be the index's, its `shape` `[rows, dimension]`, and its `data_offsets` `[0, rows × dimension × 4]` for `F32`, `× 2` for `F16`.
The data MUST be little-endian, and MUST hold no NaN or infinite value.

A host MUST reuse a set's vectors only when its own embedder's model, model digest (both absent, or equal), dimension, `dtype` and normalization all equal the index's; otherwise it MUST embed the records' text with its own model, and it MUST NOT hold two models' vectors in one index.
Vectors MUST NOT decide a walk's order or a trial's verdict; a host MAY use them in its own retrieval, which a trial then measures as any other.
